de.rule: Some verbs use de to link to what follows. Learn the verb and de together.
Adds a detail about ownership, contents, material or purpose, including an action: hora de comer = time to eat.

que.rule: Links what someone thinks, says, knows or hopes to a statement.
Means “than” when comparing people, things or situations.

se.rule: Can mean “oneself”, or belong with a verb such as sentirse (feel). It does not always mean “oneself”.
Describes what happens without naming who does it. Compare se habla (people speak) and se venden libros (books are sold).

lo.rule: With an adjective, means “the … thing” or “the … part”: lo importante = the important thing.
Refers to “him”, a masculine “it”, or an idea: lo sé = I know that.

nos.rule: Refers to us: someone sees or helps us, or tells us something.

al.rule: Here, a + el becomes al: “to the” or “at the”.
Means “when” doing something: al llegar = when someone arrives.
